#775. Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

Prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year. Now, conservationist Reshu Bashyal is leading an effort to protect them.

Words by Saugat Bolakhe and photos by CJ Karki

A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland. Beneath a canopy of pines, Himalayan chestnuts and Nepalese alders, the group listens as wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal guides them through a questionnaire designed to document the signs of poaching.

Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity. But instead of focusing on animals, as many conservation projects do, the group’s objective is to protect flora, specifically orchids. These flowering plants are harvested and sold across Nepal’s borders.

The flowers are prized for their ornamental value, but they are also used in traditional medicines, including Chinese, Tibetan and Ayurveda healing products.

Multiple parts of the plant, including the stem and fruit, can also be used as ingredients. “It’s as if these plants have some magical properties about them,” Bashyal says.

Nepal has more than 500 orchid species, many of which are heavily harvested. Between 2008 and 2016, the country legally exported more than 47,000 kilograms of wild-collected orchids. However, discrepancies exist between Nepal’s export data and those of its trading partners, arising from issues such as mismatched and unreported trade amounts and species being sold under different names.

The trade in animal and plant species is regulated mostly under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) agreement, which is designed to protect wildlife from exploitation. Although Nepal joined the convention more than 50 years ago, it did not introduce legislation to implement CITES until 2017.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

All but two species of orchid in Nepal are now listed in CITES Appendix II, which includes species that are not currently threatened with extinction but could be if their trade is not regulated. The government must create a management plan and a formal assessment to confirm that harvesting a species for trade won’t harm the survival of the wild population. “We haven’t prepared such a management plan for any orchid species yet. So, their trade is still considered illegal here,” Bashyal adds. Violation of the CITES Act can lead to a fine of up to 100,000 Nepalese rupees (US$660), one year in prison, or both.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Bashyal first became involved in orchid research by chance. In 2018, while working on a conifer tree conservation project for non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal in Kathmandu, she visited several regional sites across the country and was often approached by people asking about the demand for orchids in the city. When her team investigated further, it realized that many people living in the villages were harvesting or actively trading the plants.

This illegal trading was often overlooked by authorities, according to Bashyal. Before suggesting a way to stop it, the team had to understand the market — specifically which species were being taken, their conservation status and how the supply chain operated. To do this, it visited orchid trading hubs across Nepal and spoke to harvesters, traders and enforcement officials.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

“The local people provide information on where orchids are harvested, moved, gathered and how much they sold orchids for,” she says. During these visits, the team shared its research and spoke about the importance of conservation, which was well received, she says. “After all, an unsustainable harvesting of the orchids severely threatens local livelihood and income,” she adds.

Bashyal’s team at Greenhood Nepal learnt that several orchid species, including Satyrium nepalense and Pleione praecox, are harvested in large quantities for their medicinal value. Overharvesting an orchid species that is in decline can easily lead to its extinction in the wild, which makes understanding a species’ population and distribution crucial for creating sustainable harvesting practices.

After the field trips, Bashyal’s team created a series of policy briefs, drafted conservation frameworks and started the anti-poaching taskforce in collaboration with the region’s governmental forest management office to document illegal activity and conduct patrols.

The team is also developing comprehensive identification manuals and guidelines for regulators. Many existing manuals focus on identifying whole plants and flowers, but traded items can include the orchid’s thickened stem and fleshy underground storage organs, called tubers. Some orchids are boiled, or dried for several hours or days before being traded.

In some parts of Nepal, communities can earn a good income from harvesting and selling orchids alongside other medicinal plants. For many, medicinal plants are their sole source of income. “Simply telling the locals ‘you are not supposed to do this’ will not stop them from harvesting,” Bashyal says. For this reason, imposing a blanket ban on trade might not be effective.

Bashyal emphasizes that tracking the wildlife trade is complex and often requires navigating delicate legal territory. Researchers must also have patience when interviewing informants. “Thus, it also comes down to following research ethics, respect and treating local knowledge as a valuable resource to build trust,” Bashyal says. “Only after that, can we have data and develop any intervention.”

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

#774. Wales and West Ham's Morgan suffers serious injury

Ffion Morgan joined West Ham from Bristol City in 2025

Wales and West Ham winger Ffion Morgan is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.

Morgan has undergone surgery having been helped off during West Ham's Women's Super League win over Charlton earlier this month.

The 26-year-old is now likely to miss the rest of the season.

"Ffion will now begin her rehabilitation programme under the supervision of the club's medical team," a West Ham statement said.

The injury also makes Morgan a major doubt for next summer's Women's World Cup, should Wales qualify.

Rhian Wilkinson's side take on Norway in a two-legged play-off final next week as they bid to reach the tournament for the first time in the nation's history.

Morgan, who has 56 caps, is an international regular and would be a shoo-in for the Wales squad if fit.

Five return for Wales' World Cup play-off final

Home World Cup can inspire Wales' future stars

She joined West Ham on a two-year deal in 2025 after her contract at Bristol City expired.

Morgan has also played for Cardiff City, Coventry United and Crystal Palace.

She suffered an ACL injury while playing for Wales Under-19s as a teenager, while she had only recently returned to action for West Ham after another lengthy fitness lay-off.

Wales face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

#773. Jojo Siwa Teases Baby Plans With Boyfriend Chris Hughes

Jojo Siwa, who’s been dating boyfriend Chris Hughes for over a year, revealed her hope that her next major chapter includes becoming a mom and having a baby.

It takes two to tango, but Jojo Siwa is looking toward bigger dance numbers.

Over a year and a half after the Dance Moms alum found love with Love Island UK’s Chris Hughes, she revealed she’s ready to become a dance mom of her own.

As revealed during the Nov. 25 episode of the Petticoat Revolution podcast, her ideal next chapter would be to “have a baby. Be a mom. That’s my next thing.”

And the 23-year-old is more than ready to hit pause on her professional career in the meantime.

“Obviously that's not a career thing, but like a life thing,” she explained. “Like career, career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”

But this is not the first time Siwa has envisioned a long future with Hughes, who she met while filming Celebrity Big Brother in the UK in the spring of 2025.

n fact, Siwa previously revealed she puts her daydreams into practice when it comes to Hughes one day getting down on one knee.

“He got me this ring for Christmas last year,” Siwa told E! News of the jewelry she wore on her right hand in an interview alongside her boyfriend in October. "I wear this every day, I’ve never taken it off—sometimes I'll switch it to my other hand just see what it feels like.”

And while the 33-year-old admitted that Siwa’s trial run with an engagement ring was news to him, the revelation brought a smile to his face.

“I didn't know she did that, but now I do,” he said. “It's kind of cute.”

But sometimes, Siwa revealed, she shimmies a bit too close to the engagement sun for someone who lives so squarely in the public eye.

“I'll forget that I've done it,” she said of wearing her ring on that finger. “And I'm like, ‘Oh crap, it's been there too long. Someone's going to get a photo or something.’”

Though the couple both confirmed there aren’t any immediate plans for wedding bells to be ringing, Hughes affirmed, “One day, of course.”

As Siwa put it, “We're in a very happy phase of life right now.”

For a deeper look at Siwa and Hughes' romance, keep reading...

The couple's whirlwind romance unfolded for the whole world to see during their appearance on Celebrity Big Brother.

A year later, Siwa—who split from ex Kath Ebbs following her time on the U.K. the series—released the song "Serendipity" in honor of the now-couple's chance encounter.

"The only word to explain what happened on this day a year ago… Serendipity," Siwa wrote in an Instagram post. "Today, I’m reminded of the moment that quietly changed everything."

Less than a month after they put their bond on display in the Big Brother house and emphasizing they were just friends, Hughes and Siwa confirmed they were dating in late May 2025.

At the time, Siwa cheekily nodded at the romance during a cover of "Bette Davis Eyes" at one of her shows, in which she instead sang "Chris Hughes' eyes."

The Love Island alum joined Siwa at several stops of her Infinity Heart Tour, which spanned across Europe, the U.K. and the United States. In a sweet glimpse at their backstage moments, Siwa added of the tour in an Instagram post, "The show represents who I want to be as a person and the artist that I wanna be in this lifetime, and it’s translated so well to the crowd."

Siwa and Hughes stepped out for their first red carpet as a couple at the Dancers Against Cancer's 2025 Gala of the Stars in Beverly Hills, California.

Siwa shared a glimpse into the couple's favorite bonding activity: golfing in a sweet Instagram photo dump of her summertime adventures.

In September 2026, Hughes gave his followers a slice of life moment by filming Siwa arriving to his place in England—and naturally they shared a sweet embrace to boot.

October 2026: Coming Back Like a Boomerang

Siwa and Hughes turned the Gala of the Stars into a date night two years in a row by attending again in 2026.

Siwa proved her love for Hughes knows no bounds by teasing her next big step in life was to become a mom.

"That’s my next thing," Siwa teased during a Nov. 2026 appearance on the Petticoat Revolution podcast. "Career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”

#771. Murrell flourishing at high-flying Falkirk after 'random' move

Jacob Murrell has hit the ground running with Falkirk since his move from the United States

"It was completely random," is how Jacob Murrell describes his summer switch from DC United to Falkirk.

Now the 22 year-old American is the joint-leading scorer in the Scottish Premiership, with eight goals from 11 starts.

His tremendous form has helped Falkirk surge up the table, with six successive victories taking them from 11th to third place.

"I was looking for more minutes as a young player and Falkirk kind of came out of nowhere," he explained. "They called my agent and a week later I was in Scotland.

"It happened really fast and it was a crazy path to get here. I was just desperate to play. I wasn't happy just being a training player.

"I wanted to win games and score goals and now both are happening."

A Maryland native, the 6ft, 3in centre forward played college football at Georgetown on his way to being a super draft pick for DC United in 2024.

A big Baltimore Ravens fan, Murrell is settling into his new surroundings, although he is wary of the cuisine, telling BBC Scotland he has no plans to try haggis or black pudding.

"The first month was difficult but the club supported me the whole time, making sure I was sound and pushing me to follow my dream.

"Team-mates, staff and fans have all been so good to me and made me feel at home in such a short period of time.

"I grew up north of Baltimore and I'd been in that hour-and-a-half DC radius my entire life with my friends and family, so leaving was really hard.

"Stepping out of my comfort zone has taught me a lot about myself, having to adapt and grow up."

Murrell, the league's player of the month for October, was one of 17 summer signings made by John McGlynn, who ended the club's 15-year absence from the top flight via back-to-back promotions.

"The manager has been so good for me, instilling confidence from day one," he said. "He backs me to score goals and be an influential part of the team."

A first visit to Ibrox is next up for Murrell as Falkirk take on second-placed Rangers on Saturday.

"I'm just taking it day by day, my next focus is Rangers and trying to make it seven on the bounce," he adds.

"Things can turn fast so we need to remember where we came from, stay humble and keep working hard."

#769. Sarah Michelle Gellar Reveals Her, Freddie Prinze Jr.'s Holiday Plans

For Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr.’s family, holidays reign supreme and Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is must-see TV, she told E! while detailing her partnership with Ancestry.

Sarah Michelle Gellar knows the best way to slay the holiday season.

And for the Buffy the Vampire Slayer and husband Freddie Prinze Jr., it all comes down to focusing on their community—a tradition that dates back to her own childhood.

“A lot of times for Christmas and New Year's, we're traveling, so Thanksgiving is something that's always been important to be at home for,” Gellar told E! News in an exclusive interview. “When I was younger my mom always used to open our apartment to anyone that couldn't afford to go home or didn't have family. So, we do the same. We're actually having probably one of the largest Thanksgivings we've had in a couple years this year.”

That said, there is plenty of quiet family time amid the busy day with guests. And it’s those traditions with kids Charlotte, 17, and Rocky, 14, that have stood the test of time. In fact, Gellar admitted that when it comes to their family holiday traditions, “what's funny is they haven't really evolved” as the kids have gotten older.

“I grew up in New York City, so Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is obviously very important,” Gellar noted. “I used to go the night before and watch them blow up all the floats—you'd sit there and you'd bring your thermos of hot chocolate because it'd be freezing, and you'd watch. And so I've grown up with that parade, and I, from the time my kids were born, I'm like, we will be watching this parade."

In fact, a pre-Thanksgiving work trip to New York City was enough to have her eldest wondering if their favorite tradition might be put on pause. “When my daughter was knew I was leaving, she's like, ‘You're going to be back for the parade, right?’” Gellar revealed. “I'm like, ‘The parade's on Thanksgiving. I will be home. You don't have to worry.’ So, the Thanksgiving Day grade is always like a really big a big one for us.”

Plus, there’s the sprint to get the decorations up—and wind down with a movie marathon. On the docket this year is Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and checking out Ariana Grande in Focker-in-Law.

“Getting a tree up is always that weekend,” she explained. “Also for us going to the movies like that weekend because it's always a great movie weekend. So we've already got our tickets. We got our tickets for to see Hunger Games. We have our tickets ready to go to see Ariana in Fockers. We're ready to go."

But one tradition that never gets old for the Prinze family is taking the time to give back.

“I didn't grow up with a lot,” the Cruel Intentions actress shared. “I had a single mom, and we did the best we could. But my mom always wanted to remind me to be grateful for my situation because there are children that were so much less fortunate. So we used to every year go to the post office and get a secret Santa.”

And it wound up being a formative experience. “Even at a young age, I clocked that these kids weren't asking for the Cabbage Patch Kid that I wanted,” Gellar recalled. “They were asking for shoes that didn't have holes in them or a jacket that fit—that first realization that there's real need out there and that you can make a difference. And even though you know we couldn't, I wanted to fill every Christmas list that was there, and my mom would have to explain to me like we can do as many as we can within reason.”

She added, “But just being a part of making that child's Christmas or that family's Christmas, they ask for diapers, they ask for these things, and so that sort of always stuck with me.”

In fact, she’s continued to pay it forward, teaming up with Ancestry for its Gathering the Good initiative, inspiring people to take a peek at the history of giving in their own life while also helping those in need this holiday season.

The spirit of giving is also a trait she and Prinze are passing on to their teens.

“I just love watching the joy that it brings to my kids to be able to see that they can make a difference in someone's life," she noted. "I want someone to always remember there's always something you can do. And you know maybe it's not financial, maybe it's giving your time.”

Put simply, “There's so much you can do to make someone else's life a little bit easier, and in turn, it makes your life easier because you're just that little bit happier.”

For a look back at Gellar and Prinze's sweetest memories with their kids, keep reading...

Driving home the fact that son Rocky looks just like dad Freddie Prinze Jr., Sarah Michelle Gellar shared a photo from a "race weekend with my boys" in October 2026.

The actress celebrated the aspiring F1 driver completing another lap around the sun and turning 14. "I should have known from your speedy delivery, the excitement you would bring," she wrote on Instagram in September 2026. "You have no idea how lucky I feel to watch you chase your dream. You inspire not just me, but everyone around you."

Sarah also paid tribute to her "best friend" and daughter Charlotte, who was born three years and one day prior to her little brother."I’m not sure how you are 17 already," the Buffy the Vampire Slayer star shared on Instagram in September 2026. "You may have been the child that made me a mom, but now you are the person that brings out the best in me. (Not to mention my biggest champion) Thank you… for being you."

Not switching gears, Rocky's mom shared a heartfelt post when he turned 13."Aside from being one of the fastest in the state, you are one of the most polite, kind and funny kids I know," she penned on Instagram in September 2025. "I can’t believe you are a teenager. I love you more than my words can express!!!"

As the sun set on an old year and rose on a new, Sarah, Freddie and the kids enjoyed a trip to Hawaii—with her posting a "vacation dump" in January 2024.

Fans know what this crew did that summer. The I Know What You Did Last Summer costars took their children on a trip to Italy in July 2023.

Sarah's intentions for this adorable throwback? To celebrate Rocky's birthday!"Your laugh is infectious, your jokes are the best and your spirit is … EVERYTHING," the Cruel Intentions alum raved on Instagram in September 2023. "You make every day brighter."

Making a rare red carpet appearance, Charlotte joined her mom at the L.A. screening of Sarah's movie Do Revenge in September 2022.

Scooby-Dooby-Doo, where are you? The Scooby-Doo costars and their children returned to Hawaii to say goodbye to 2021 and hello to 2022.

For Charlotte's birthday in 2021, Sarah reflected on how "this day 12 years ago my greatest life truly began."

And on Rocky's 9th birthday that year, the Ringer celeb looked back at when he was born and his parents' "hearts exploded."

This 2019 photo of Charlotte starting fourth grade and Rocky beginning first is one for the books.

Sarah gave a shout-out to her husband on Father's Day 2016."The greatest part of every day is watching life through my children's eyes," she wrote on Instagram, "so today (and every day) Freddie I thank you."

After Charlotte was cast as baby Simba in a children's production of The Lion King, her mom shared a snap of her using Freddie's binder to study lines."So no matter how hard we have tried (and believe me we have tried) to convince our daughter to find any hobby but performing, she has shown a great love (and talent) for being on the stage," Sarah wrote on Instagram in 2016 before joking, "(wonder where she gets that from?)."

"In my household cooking is family time, time to #unplug and connect," the cookbook author wrote on Instagram in 2015 alongside a photo of her and her little ones. "I treasure these moments."

#768. SFA to deliver revised proposal after young player vote delayed

The Scottish FA says they will continue consulting with SPFL clubs in a bid to get more game time for homegrown talent after initial plans put forward by the governing body failed to reach a member vote.

Following an all-club meeting at St Andrews in September, the SFA proposed financial incentives - and penalties - along with quotas, in a bid to get more youngsters playing for clubs.

Initially, these proposals were to have been voted on at a SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's annual meeting this month.

But the SFA now say they are aiming to put refreshed proposals to the clubs in the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of the 2027-28 season.

Despite the governing body saying they are "encouraged", they add that "recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation."

"The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews," a Scottish FA statement read.

"We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game."

"It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams."

'Not fit for purpose' - Craig Mulholland on youth pathway

Craig Mulholland, SFA chief football officer, has engaged with clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, however media speculation suggests those plans may have been diluted.

At their initial consultation with clubs, they put forward three suggestions to increase minutes for young Scottish players:

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Scottish Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Premier Sports Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Clubs should field Scotland-eligible Under-21 players for an average of 60 minutes in each game across all four SPFL divisions (6% of available minutes).

The proposals were introduced following a dramatic dip in Scottish-born players being played by Premiership clubs and suggestions of a fear by managers and owners to take a chance on academy players.

Statistics also reflect a huge increase in young players being tempted south to club academies in England, prompting widespread concerns they could be lost in a vast youth system rather than breaking into first teams domestically.

"Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right," the governing body adds.

#767. 'I persuaded my club to give me a job as a content creator'

Making videos with fans and players at his local football club is all in a day's work for Jacob.

He's a content creator for Bolton Wanderers FC, he comes up with new ideas for social media, filming videos and posts them onto official pages. The aim is to encourage people to follow the club.

There are many different ways to develop a career in football content creation, from apprenticeships to freelance work and full-time employment. It isn't just about making videos - content creators need to understanding their audience, respond to analytics and adapt material for different platforms

Jacob works as a content creator for Bolton Wanderers and his career progression has followed this path:

Voluntary work at Bolton --> Professional content creator

While it might look simple, he's had to be resilient - and one of the biggest obstacles he faced was convincing Bolton to create his role. "Don't wait for an opportunity to come to you," he says. "If you're good at it, it does then sometimes lead into getting a role. If it doesn't, you've created a portfolio and it's really good for your CV and future opportunities."

Jacob says salaries can range from Â£26,000 to around Â£40,000 for roles like his. Like him, some content creators start by doing it as a hobby while they improve their skills. While some content creators are full-time employees, many are freelancers so their average salaries can be variable.

Find out more about the role of a content creator below. Content creation roles can come under a range of titles including social media manager or content manager.

You could get into this role via a college course (to get practical skills in video editing and production, or a T Level in Marketing), an apprenticeship, volunteering, short private training courses and also teaching yourself.

This information is a guide and is constantly changing. Please check the National Careers Service website for the latest information and all the qualifications needed and the GOV.UK website for more on T-levels.

#766. Travis Kelce Teases NFL Future After 100th Game at Arrowhead Stadium

Travis Kelce addressed his plans on returning for another NFL season with the Kansas City Chiefs following his historic 100th home game at Arrowhead Stadium.

Travis Kelce is not ready to say so long, Arrowhead.

After the Kansas City Chiefs tight end marked his 100th regular season home game on Nov. 22, he teased his NFL future while addressing his post-game pledge of “cheers to 100 more.”

“You’re not gonna play a f--kin’ 100 more games. What are you talkin’ about?” his brother Jason Kelce joked on the Nov. 25 episode of their New Heights podcast, calling out Travis. “What are you talkin’ about?”

“Yeah, you’re right, I won’t,” Travis replied. “But cheers to 100 more.”

He hinted that his final huddle may not be on the horizon. As the 36-year-old—who married Taylor Swift in July—put it, “Who knows how many I’ll get to?”

But when his older brother asked him if he was “confirming” he’ll be returning for another season, Travis paused and sighed, before replying, “No. I’m not confirming it.”

And though the athlete—who has played for the Chiefs throughout his 14 seasons in the NFL and signed a two-year contract in 2024—is keeping his football future under wraps for now, he’s continuing to celebrate his historic game at Arrowhead Stadium last weekend.

“One hundred games, dude, it feels pretty awesome right now,” Travis shared. “To think about that legacy of that stadium and it’s pretty crazy to think they’re moving on from that stadium, because of all the history that’s happened over the years and history of the franchise and everything.”

And though the Chiefs will be leaving the stadium in 2031, Travis’ memories at Arrowhead go beyond football. After all, it’s where his romance with Taylor began after he attended her Eras Tour concert at the venue in 2023.

“It’s been home for me for 14 years,” Travis expressed. “It’s been one of my favorite places to go to play and to watch not only football, but musical events and I’ve had so much history and so many things that mean so much to me happen at Arrowhead that a 100 games, it’s pretty awesome to hit that milestone.”

But that wasn’t the NFL star’s only achievement during Nov. 22 face-off against the Arizona Cardinals as Travis scored a touchdown in the first quarter, officially putting him into the third-place slot for most career touchdowns by a tight end.

And his loved ones were there cheering him on, with Taylor celebrating the exciting moment with Travis’ niece Wyatt Kelce, the eldest daughter of Jason and his wife Kylie Kelce’s four kids.

In fact, not only has Grammy winner established herself as quite the cheer captain, but she’s become “fully engulfed” in the sport, according to her husband.

“Now she knows everything,” Travis shared on a September episode of New Heights. “She sees the flags coming in, like, ‘Oh, that might be a defensive hold.’ [I’m] like, ‘What’d you say, sweetie?’ She’s like, ‘That’s encroachment.’ I’m like, ‘You know what that is?’”

For a closer look at the couple’s touchdown-worthy romance, keep reading…

Long before Taylor Swift's attendance at the Kansas City Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 game became one of the definitive pop culture moments of the year, Travis Kelce was an admirer of the Grammy winner.

The star tight end's interest in Taylor was first revealed by one of his teammates in a TikTok video posted by the Chiefs in August 2023 (which, in hindsight, was when the pair were secretly dating).

Before Travis could answer the prompt of who his celebrity crush was, wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling spilled, "Taylor Swift!"

Travis smiled at the camera before holding his finger up to his mustache, saying, "Alright now!"

Plus, Travis was just one of many celebs to attend Taylor's record-breaking Eras Tour even before the now-engaged duo kicked off their romance. But more on that enchanting moment in a bit...

No. 2: He's Not Her Usual Type (on Paper)

While he does have that daydream look in his eyes (especially when he sees Taylor on the big-screen at one of his games), Travis stands out a bit when you look back at Taylor’s dating history.

She is typically attracted to creative types, including actors (Joe Alwyn, Jake Gyllenhaal, Taylor Lautner and Tom Hiddleston) and musicians (Calvin Harris, John Mayer, Harry Styles and, most recently, Matty Healy).

But perhaps that’s why her romance with the lighthearted and cheeky athlete—who signed an updated two-year deal with the Chiefs worth $34.25 million in 2024—feels like such a refreshing option for Taylor after her six-year uber-private relationship with Joe came to an end in April 2023.

Looks like the 10-time Pro Bowler’s wishes came true after he all but manifested his romance with the superstar through sheer will, determination and declarations of infatuation.

Travis publicly aired his failed attempt to shoot his shot and talk to Taylor when he attended the Kansas City stop on her Eras Tour July 7, 2023. As it turns out, he had a special gift for her: A friendship bracelet bearing his "number" that he hoped to give Taylor. (He wouldn't definitively say if it was his jersey number or phone number.)

Despite his claim that he was "disappointed" he failed to meet her after the concert, Taylor confirmed to TIME in December 2023 that she belatedly caught his podcast pass.

"Travis very adorably put me on blast on his podcast, which I thought was metal as hell," she recalled. "We started hanging out right after that. So we actually had a significant amount of time that no one knew, which I'm grateful for, because we got to get to know each other."

So, that whole theory about the Sept. 24 game being their first official hang? As Taylor clarified to TIME, "We would never be psychotic enough to hard launch a first date."

Since dating Travis, Taylor has been seen in public more frequently, including outings with friends in NYC and jubilant appearances at award shows, like the 2023 MTV VMAs and the 2024 Grammys.

But her most talked-about appearance? Sitting in Travis' suite at the Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 home game against the Chicago Bears.

Rather than shy away from the attention, Taylor cheered and screamed "Let's f--king go!" when Travis scored a touchdown. Like the public, even Travis admitted he was caught off-guard by Taylor accepting his invite.

"Shoutout to Taylor for pulling up, that was pretty ballsy," Travis said days later on his New Heights podcast. "I just thought it was awesome how everyone in the suite had nothing but great things to say about her, the friends and family."

"She looked amazing," he added. " It was definitely a game I will remember, that's for damn sure."

Since then, Taylor and Travis have been photographed hand-in-hand on dates all around the world and have made multiple visits to a Christmas bar in Kansas City, where they were not shy about PDA.

And, after revealing to TIME that she retreated from the spotlight when Kim Kardashian's infamous leaked phone call in 2016, Taylor is going out tonight...and every night, if she wants to, thank you very much.

"Life is short," she said. "Have adventures. Me locking myself away in my house for a lot of years—I’ll never get that time back. I’m more trusting now than I was six years ago.”

While Travis isn't afraid to spill some tea on his Sept. 27, 2023 podcast regarding his interactions with Taylor, he still expressed his boundaries about addressing his personal life moving forward.

"I know I brought all this attention to me," he explained. "I did the whole friendship bracelet thing and told everyone how butthurt I was that I didn't get to meet Taylor." However, he continued, he didn't plan to give a full play-by-play of their relationship.

"What's real is that it is my personal life and I want to respect both of our lives," he explained. "I'm enjoying life and I sure as hell enjoyed this weekend. So everything moving forward, I think me talking about sports and saying 'alright nah' will have to be where I keep it."

He doubled-down on his desire to play it cool in a November 2023 interview with the Wall Street Journal.

"Everybody around me telling me: Don't f--k this up! And me sitting here saying: Yeah—got it," he told the outlet, before addressing the media attention. "That was the biggest thing to me: make sure I don't say anything that would push Taylor away."

But that doesn't mean he's been able to resist publicly talking about his girlfriend—crediting her for the boost in sales of his jersey and calling her "amazing" after she was booed by New England Patriots fans at a December 2023 game.

"I've never been a man of words," he admitted to WSJ. "Being around her, seeing how smart Taylor is, has been f--king mind-blowing. I'm learning every day."

Like Taylor, who is close with her parents, particularly her mother Andrea, Travis hails from a tight-knit fam, including his parents Ed and Donna Kelce.

Donna became a beloved public figure as the first mother to have two sons playing against each other in a Super Bowl, when Travis faced off against his older brother, Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, in the big game in February 2023.

"For all the stars to align and for them to get through high school and college and the pros. And for them to both play in the Pro Bowl and to play in the Super Bowl, and then for this to happen," Donna told ET at the time. "This is just like a dream come true. I can't express enough how special this is for the family and it's just crazy."

Donna, who was married to Ed for 25 years before they divorced, supported both of her sons by wearing a half-black, half-red Eagles and Chiefs jacket.

After the Super Bowl, which saw the Chiefs best the Eagles, Travis and Jason got emotional while reflecting on sharing the experience with Donna.

"The moment I saw mom is when I got really emotional," Jason said on the brothers' New Heights podcast. "It was so awesome...She was on top of the world for a week."

"She was the heavyweight champ man," Travis added. "She was on top of it, and she shined the whole time."

Like Taylor and her younger brother Austin Swift, Travis has a special bond with his older brother Jason, who inspired him to play football.

In addition to their impressive careers as NFL players, Travis and Jason launched their podcast New Heights in September 2022, a project that has only strengthened their relationship (and their bank accounts).

"What this did was gave us a scheduled two to three hour window where we have to talk to each other and we have to talk about what we're going through, throughout the week and throughout the games," Travis told NBC Sports in February 2023. "It's almost been like therapy, man."

Sure, the pair technically never met until 2023, but there have been a few invisible strings tying them together.

Taylor and Travis both count Miles Teller as a friend, with the Top Gun: Maverick star and his wife Keleigh Sperry even being recruited by Taylor to star in the music video for "I Bet You Think About Me" off Red (Taylor's Version) in 2021.

Travis, meanwhile, joined Miles and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes for golfing practice ahead of the American Century Championship in 2022.

Miles tweeted a photo of himself on the golf course with the athletes, writing, "Grip it and rip it." Travis proved the bromance was real when he reposted the shot and added, "Back at it like we never left!!"

(Interestingly enough, Miles is a noted diehard Philadelphia Eagles fans, so perhaps he put in a word with Jason to broker an IRL meet-up between Travis and Taylor?)

While Taylor attended the Sept. 24, 2023 game solo, she brought an entourage of celebrity friends with her when she attended the Chiefs' match-up against the New York Jets at New Jersey's Metlife Stadium on Oct. 1.

She was accompanied by BFFs Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds and his friend Hugh Jackman, as well as Sophie Turner, Sabrina Carpenter and Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski.

While their attendance at the game spoke volumes, even more telling was Ryan following Travis on Instagram.

Not only has Travis played in four Super Bowls, winning three of them (NBD!), but he's also hosted Saturday Night Live, so you know he can handle intense spotlight with ease.

That may seem trivial, but Taylor has penned several songs regarding her fear that her level of fame could prove to be too much for her romantic partner to handle. (See: "Peace" and "The Archer.")

"It all depends who you're with," Taylor said in, "If they have a serious issue with it, I guess you'll hide or whatever, but I don't really like that, because it makes me feel like I'm running from the law or something. I don't want to feel like a fugitive, like, 'Oh my god, we're having a relationship, better hide!'

"I feel like if you can be in a relationship and have it seem normal, that would be good."

And in his WSJ interview, Travis proved he's more than ready for the pressure that comes with being married to someone as powerful as Taylor.

"Obviously I've never dated anyone with that kind of aura about them...I've never dealt with it," he said. "But at the same time, I'm not running away from any of it."

"The scrutiny she gets, how much she has a magnifying glass on her, every single day, paparazzi outside her house, outside every restaurant she goes to, after every flight she gets off, and she's just living, enjoying life," he added. "When she acts like that I better not be the one acting all strange."

Further proving their love is worthy of a rom-com treatment, fans were swooning after a concertgoer captured video of Taylor running into Travis' arms and exchanging a passionate kiss after performing in Argentina in November 2023. And that was after she changed the lyrics in Karma from "the guy on the screen" to "the guy on the Chiefs," much to Travis' surprise as he attended alongside her father, Scott Swift.

Turning out for one another's stadium takeovers—Taylor attended 13 Chiefs games her first season with Travis, traveling straight from her Tokyo show to make the Super Bowl—is a show of how serious their relationship is.

"I'm going to see him do what he loves, we're showing up for each other, other people are there and we don't care," Taylor told TIME of their public support. "The opposite of that is you have to go to an extreme amount of effort to make sure no one knows that you're seeing someone. And we're just proud of each other."

And if her presence at the NFL games annoys you, well, Taylor can't even be bothered to have bad blood with you.

"There's a camera, like, a half-mile away, and you don't know where it is, and you have no idea when the camera is putting you in the broadcast, so I don't know if I'm being shown 17 times or once," she said. "I'm just there to support Travis. I have no awareness of if I'm being shown too much and pissing off a few dads, Brads, and Chads."

Travis was born in—are you ready for it?—1989. Screaming, crying, throwing up, etc.

Speaking of Killa Trav's birthday, which falls on October 5, did you know he shares his with Taylor's late grandmother Marjorie Finlay, the subject of her song "Marjorie" off of 2020's evermore? If we didn't know better, we'd think this is a sign...

She's loved him three summers now, honey, and she's going to get 'em all.

#765. How to become a football referee

Honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

Have you always been passionate about football?

Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

Becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and said sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

What subjects did you study at school and university?

Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your plan and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

With a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:

In her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees new referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she says. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared."

All four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

Louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she says. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

As well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful."

You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

After Julianne Hough and Peloton instructor Adrian Williams's breakup, the Dancing With the Stars co-host shared a cryptic message to her Instagram account about trust.

Julianne Hough is tangoing with matters of the heart.

After the Dancing With the Stars co-host revealed that she and Peloton instructor Adrian Williams had broken up, she posted a series of photos and cryptic messages to social media, putting her feelings center stage.

“The highest currency is not attention," read one image reshared to Hough's Instagram Story Nov. 25, "it's trust."

Earlier, the 38-year-old posted another text-only post to her Stories that said, “May you attract someone who pours as much love and care into you as you pour into them.”

The 42-year-old posted a photo of the dachshund during a walk to his Instagram Stories Nov. 25.

And when his split from Hough was confirmed, Williams shared his own cryptic message, reposting a photo from his motivational account that included a picture of him in his car with a text-only photo that read, “Your reset doesn’t have to make sense to anyone else. Mine has three pedals.”

#763. Taylor and Lewis suffer five straight defeats on Modus Super Series return

Phil Taylor came out of retirement to partner Adrian Lewis for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth, but the duo endured a disappointing return, losing all five of their matches; Taylor retired from professional darts in 2018

Phil 'The Power' Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffered five losses from five matches for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth.

Taylor, now 66, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after claiming his 16th and final world title. However, the 16-time world champion returned to action to partner his long-time friend Lewis for the tournament.

Their opening match on Thursday saw them face Scotland's John Henderson and Robert Thornton, with the England pair suffering a narrow 4-3 defeat.

Things failed to improve in their second outing, as Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-2 by Sweden's Andreas Harrysson and Anton Ostlund.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

A shock 4-3 defeat to unheralded Swiss duo Ansh Sood and Marcel Walpen followed, before Taylor and Lewis suffered a fourth consecutive loss, going down 4-1 to Germany's Daniel Klose and Liam Maendl-Lawrance.

Their fifth and final group-stage outing saw England take a 2-1 lead against Denmark, the only other side in their pool yet to record a victory. However, Ivan Springborg Poulsen and Andreas Toft Jorgensen responded by winning the next three legs in succession to condemn the English pair to a 4-2 defeat and a fifth straight loss.

Taylor revealed in September that the opportunity to partner Lewis was enough to tempt him back to the oche, although his return is not expected to signal a permanent comeback.

The 16-time world champion, who recently underwent successful hip replacement surgery, previously enjoyed considerable success alongside Lewis, with the pair winning four World Cup of Darts titles together.

The Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament continues in Portsmouth until November 28.

#762. 'My job combines my passion for gaming and football'

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

We're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

Growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a new build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

So even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save."

So as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

So I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a new job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

One of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

#761. Barbara Eden Reveals the Workout Routine That Keeps Her Fit at 95

I Dream of Jeannie’s Barbara Eden revealed the workout regimen she follows in order to keep her healthy and moving at 95 years old.

Barbara Eden does much more than think and blink, even as a nonagenarian.

In fact, at 95 years old the I Dream of Jeannie alum’s fitness routine includes more than those of some people decades younger than her.

"I go for about, I don't know, 35 minutes on the bike," Eden told Fox News Digital of her main exercise these days, which occurs on a stationary bike. "It's good."

And though she doesn’t go to the gym anymore, her previous routine involved “spinning class for an hour,” she explained, “and then I worked with a trainer for a half hour, lifting weights."

But she hasn’t completely put down the weights, though she doesn’t lift quite as heavy as she used to.

For Eden, staying healthy through fitness has long been a personal wish she’s happy to grant.

“You have to be disciplined about being active when you’re an actor," Eden—married to Jon Eicholtz since 1991—said. "My husband and I both have a trainer that comes in and helps us out."

Despite her disciplined routine, however, the Flaming Star actress can’t pinpoint just one source of her longevity.

Nevertheless, “I'm glad I'm here,” she said. “And I'm glad I'm still working."

She does, of course, try to make healthy choices—within reason.

"I'm careful about what I eat, but I'm not overly stupid about it, you know?" she said. "I've never smoked. I don't know if that means anything.”

As for skincare? While Eden emphasized using sunscreen, she said her own routine is only two steps: washing her face at night followed by moisturizer. As she noted, “That’s about it.”

For Eden, however, her philosophy about wellness goes beyond the personal and the physical, with external connection being a constant priority.

“I think one of the things that's most important in your life is that you recognize other people,” she mused. “You realize that they're not so different than you are and that you have to get along. And when you do that, you find life is much more interesting, and people are much more interesting."

"Eventually, if you dedicate yourself to it, you will have lived your life longer with this habit than you ever did without it. At least, that's the way I like to think about it."

#760. Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2

The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

Russian  ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown — killed two people and wounded dozens of others, local officials said Saturday.

The attacks come amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine, on three occasions this week, struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to the Kerch attack, as the bridge is vital for war supplies for Russian forces in the south.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Among the dead in Friday evening's double-tap strikes on Kryvyi Rih were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while several children were among the 60 wounded, the Ukrainian officials said.

Several fires broke out and damage was caused to about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram.

Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia's Defense Ministry said a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.

Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow said was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.

Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday.

One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.

In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, said it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity."

After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway."

#758. Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards)

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards)

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension)

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension)

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension)

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension)

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension)

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension)

#756. When is the Nations League quarter-final draw?

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June

#755. Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League

Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games

Manchester City sported a new orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.

Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their new kit.

However, there is no limit in the Champions League, meaning City can wear their new strip for the rest of their European campaign.

City can also wear the kit in the FA Cup, provided that an application is made to the Football Association, as well as a reason for its requested use.

That is why Arsenal were allowed to play in a white fourth strip in the 2025-26 FA Cup as part of their campaign to combat youth knife crime in London.

Fans could scan the badge on City's 2025-26 fourth kit to receive items in a video game

City also released a green fourth kit in 2025-26 with a gaming-inspired theme.

The kit, debuted during their Champions League victory over Villarreal, featured an NFC chip in the club badge that fans could scan to unlock gaming rewards.

The club released another fourth kit in the 2024-25 season co-designed by Noel Gallagher in tribute to the 30th anniversary of Oasis' 1994 album 'Definitely Maybe'.

It was worn in the Champions League by the men's team against Inter Milan and Paris St-Germain, and the women's team against Paris FC and Barcelona.

A fifth kit was also used by the men's team during the 2025 Club World Cup

During the 2023-24 season, the women's side also sported a Chinese New Year-inspired shirt in a League Cup victory against rivals Manchester United.

While the Premier League is more restrictive over the number of kits that can be released - the rules are more relaxed in other European leagues.

Napoli wore 13 strips during the 2021-22 season; including a Halloween kit, four different Diego Maradona tributes and four Europa League-specific kits.

#754. Joan Smalls Says Tom Brady Was "Catalyst" for Candice Swanepoel Feud

Joan Smalls addressed her and fellow Victoria's Secret Angel Candice Swanepoel's friendship fallout, confirming that the South African model's new romance with Tom Brady was the reason.

Joan Smalls is strutting away from relationships that don't respect girl code.

One month after rumors emerged that the Victoria's Secret supermodel was unhappy with fellow runway star Candice Swanepoel for dating her former fling Tom Brady, she confirmed the New England Patriots alum was at the center of their friendship breakup.

"Unfortunately, that was the catalyst," Smalls said during the Nov. 25 episode of The Cutting Room Floor podcast. "I was seeing this person for a period of eight months."

E! News has reached out to reps for Swanepoel and Brady for comment and has not yet heard back.

Though Smalls doesn't consider Brady to be an ex, she clarified that they casually dated the former NFL star on and off between 2023 and 2024. Swanepoel went on to spark romance rumors with Brady in June.

And for her part, Smalls emphasized that before ending her and Swanepoel's 15-year friendship—which she confirmed took place in April—they were each other's confidants about love and heartbreak.

"You've seen the relationships, situationships and people I've dated, and I've confided in you in these spaces and we never had a crossover," she reflected. "All of a sudden, I stopped seeing this person, and three months later, you text me and say, 'Oh, we have to speak about something,' which is usually not a conversation we normally have."

The Puerto Rican-born model—who had confirmed their fallout in scathing comments under her own Instagram posts last month—had a feeling that Swanepoel, 38, was planning to name him her MVP.

"I called her and I asked her, I said, 'Is this about him?' She said, 'Yes,'" she recalled. "We spoke on the phone very briefly, and I was just perplexed and lost for words."

The confrontation was especially devastating because Smalls said Swanepoel—who was previously linked to model Andrés Velencoso in 2022—had been a guiding light during her romance with the Fox Sports commentator.

"She helped me write text messages to this person," Smalls, also 38, said. "She knew intimate things. Potentially to my detriment, I overshared. I was just being open with a friend that I thought was a safe spac

As for how the conversation went? Smalls accused her former friend of committing a cardinal girl code sin: Dating a guy your friend was romantically involved with.

"She came across as justifying her actions," she explained. "She started diminishing my experience to make herself feel better about the situation, which I think is what infuriated me."

Smalls believed that Swanepoel—who shares two sons with ex Hermann Nicoli—refused to take accountability for being a bad friend.

"It was this whole attitude of 'I'm an adult. I don't need permission,'" she posited. "Both are actually true: you are an adult and you don't need permission. But as a friend, you should consider me in your choices. Don't consider me in your apologies."

"Then she was like, 'Well, I'm sorry, but I'm going to explore this and so is life,'" she continued. "It was just this attitude of entitlement and lack of care towards someone who's your friend and something that I would never do to you."

Looking back at the conversation, Smalls felt that Swanepoel was looking to ease her own mind.

As she put it, "She wanted me to comfort her about her bad decision so that she didn't feel guilty by her choice and then she would constantly justify it."

It was especially difficult for the model since she prefers to keep her inner circle small.

"I rarely allow people into my life, and I'm very private," Smalls added. "So, if I let you into a space that I thought you would protect me as my friend, that's the only one thing I asked for you to do. Create a safe space for me to be myself, to open up, and you can't do that."

Following initial speculations about their fallout, Swanepoel's team detailed her perspective on their friendship.

"Candice has always been exceptionally private about her personal life, with her focus remaining on raising her children," her rep Amanda Ruisi told E! News in October. "She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect."

As Smalls and Swanepoel navigate life after their friendship, keep reading for more famous celebrity feuds.

That many years spent doing something so special that people had a connection with is such a privileged."

During a 2022 TikTok challenge, JoJo Siwa described Candace Cameron Bure as the "rudest" celebrity, later explaining that she felt snubbed when Bure once refused to take a picture with her on a red carpet. #753. Why are there 2:05pm kick-offs in the Premier League on Sunday?

Everton's derby with Liverpool has been moved from Saturday to Sunday

The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.

Everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day. The game was originally scheduled for Saturday.

This has had a knock-on effect on the remaining fixtures.

On a typical Premier League weekend, the first matches will begin at 14:00 followed by a final 16:30 kick-off.

Pushing start times back five minutes to 14:05 reduces the risk of overlap with the unusual early 12:00 start time, while avoiding clashing with the 16:30 fixture.

Midweek European games have also affected the schedule, as the Premier League aims to prevent clubs from playing two matches within 60 hours of each other.

Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton are all set to play in the Europa and Conference Leagues on Thursday, ruling them out of Saturday Premier League fixtures.

#752. Eckert: Time to 'close the chapter' on Spygate ahead of Boro reunion

Tonda Eckert speaks to Sky Sports News reporter Mark McAdam about 'Spygate' fallout, their points deduction and reunion with Middlesbrough. Watch Southampton vs Middlesbrough live on Sky Sports Football from 7.30pm on Friday night; kick-off 8pm.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"I think we've experienced a little bit more in the last 12 months than normal."

It may be the understatement of the century, but it's not a huge surprise considering Tonda Eckert is a relatively understated man.

The storm of 'Spygate' is over, but the aftershock is still being felt. Southampton are sixth in the table, seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough ahead of their reunion on Friday night - live on Sky Sports.

Were it not for the four-point deduction, the gap would be smaller. Were it not for the entire controversy, the Saints would possibly be in the Premier League right now.

Eckert knows he broke the rules, and is thankful for the club and the support-base for backing him. Something that wouldn't have been easy after the ignominy of being kicked out of the play-offs.

"There have been some points, especially over the summer, where I think the club has made a commitment that not many clubs would have made," he admits.

"I'm very grateful, first of all, for the opportunity to step up in the first place, but also for the support over the summer. Obviously, that goes from everyone in the building to our supporters.

"This summer has been the biggest test we can possibly have in terms of the relationship between a football club and a fan base, and a manager and a fan base. I think the supporters have been great. It's been a tough period for them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"Towards the end of last season, it was difficult to process for everyone because of the process we used. I would have wanted to address the supporters a little earlier, so it took almost two weeks before I got to speak to them.

"From there on, I think the commitment has been very clear. It started with the football club and some players who committed to the project.

"You could just sense, the closer we got to the season, that everyone wanted to leave that behind and show what we are about as a football club and how much joy we bring when we go on the pitch. We felt that throughout the summer and on the first day of training.

"To come out of that situation with new strength just shows what this football club is about. Now it's for us to look forward and make sure that we continue to do that.

"There was still some uncertainty for the first block of games, and you just need to find a way, for me and obviously for everyone else in the football club, to put that to the side. As soon as the season starts, you need to perform.

"Then, obviously, to close that chapter finally, we needed a decision from the club. I think that's helped us to close that chapter."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The uncertainty came from the FA investigation, which wasn't resolved until October. In the end he was given a fine and a suspended six-week ban.

"Obviously, it's never easy to work on a daily basis if you have some uncertainty, and that's not just for me," he says. "I think it's the same for everyone at the football club.

"But I think we found a way, even in the first block of games, to perform. There's always something going on in football, sometimes a little bit bigger and sometimes not as big, but you need to push that to the side and make sure you find a way to perform.

"Once the decision came, I think it was important for everyone that we could finally close that."

For Eckert and Southampton it is just about points on the board, now. Trying to make up the deficit they were dealt at the start of the season.

"Obviously, if you could choose, no one would choose to start the season on minus four points," he says. "That's what it is. I think we are strong enough to make our way forward in the table.

"You shouldn't underestimate us coming from behind. We've shown that we are able to chase teams down, and that's the job for this year.

"It's been important for us to get some points on the board early in the season. We are still not where we want to be towards the end, so we need to make sure we continue."

Last week, Southampton handed Eckert, still just 33, a contract extension until 2029. They clearly feel he is their man to get them back to where they want to be.

"I think we've always been very open with our ambitions," he says. "There's no point in hiding that.

"I think the conditions are there to go up. It's never easy, but it's for us now to finish the job."
