#733. Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace

Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

A Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace, the Nordic country's Ministry of Defense said Saturday.

The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.

According to Finland's Defense Ministry, the incursion happened at 12:34 p.m. local time (10:34 UTC/GMT) off the town of Loviisa, on the southern coast.

"This alleged airspace violation may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations carried out by Finland following damage sustained by a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland," public broadcaster YLE cited Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen as saying.

The ministry added the helicopter could have penetrated up to 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.

Earlier Saturday, Finland — one of NATO's newest members — said a Russian cargo ship heading for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad caught fire after being struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.

The Finnish military said the Sparta II was damaged ⁠west ⁠of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters.

Finnish ‌Border ​Guard Commander Ilja Iljin later told YLE that the vessel, which is known to have links to the Russian military, was struck by Ukrainian  drones while in Russian waters.

"At the moment, ​there is no confirmed information ⁠about ​what cargo ​is on board, ​but it ‌cannot be ruled out ​that ⁠there is military materiel on ⁠board," ​Iljin said.

The ship is on a US sanctions list, according to a search of the Open Sanctions website.

The Border Guard later said the crew of the Sparta II was evacuating into a life raft and rescue boat.

"The [Ukraine] war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas," wrote Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on X.

Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," he added.

The Finnish government has put temporary curbs on aviation and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

The Defense Ministry said Finland had informed its allies about the incident.

#732. One of football's most-hyped 16-year-olds - what next for JJ Gabriel?

JJ Gabriel featured for Manchester United's senior team in pre-season

It has been one of the biggest transfer sagas of the year - around a player who has never played competitive football.

Forward JJ Gabriel, who has recently turned 16, walked out on Manchester United in September and now has a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

Before even playing a senior game - barring friendlies - he has told Spanish newspaper Marca his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or".

Gabriel's real name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill - with Cypriot and Irish lineage - but he changed his name, reportedly for commercial purposes.

His father, London-born Joe O'Cearuill, played twice for the Republic of Ireland - but the highest level he played at club level was a loan spell with Brighton in League One and one minute in the Uefa Cup with St Patrick's Athletic. He has been actively involved in his son's career.

Gabriel was scheduled to become Manchester United's youngest ever player in the Carabao Cup against Brighton on 16 September, but had told the club he planned to leave by then.

How long will Gabriel have to wait for a first-team debut now? In the past 10 years Real have only handed two debuts to 17-year-olds and none to a 16-year-old.

When Real boss Jose Mourinho was asked about Gabriel on Friday, he said: "I don't have a feeling [about Gabriel]. I don't have a feeling with players who don't work with me."

In fact, Real have not even announced anything yet - despite Gabriel posting a 50-second video montage on social media saying goodbye to United this week.

Madrid-bound Gabriel posts farewell Man Utd message

Why schoolboys have become a huge part of football's transfer market

For a while now Madrid have been getting the best young talents early and turning them into Galacticos before they cost in excess of 100m euros.

Vinicius Junior and Rodrygo came that way, then Endrick - and Gabriel is seen as the next.

It fits the policy run by Jose Angel Sanchez, the director general, and Juni Calafat, head of scouting. It is a long-term bet on one of the most promising young players in the international game.

Barcelona looked at him too, and backed away because the commissions were too high. Madrid believe in the player so much that they were willing to pay whatever it took to get the deal done.

The expectations are very high and the aim is for him to reach the first team. They want him at Castilla - Real's reserve team - but the situation right now does not allow it.

Castilla and Real Madrid C cannot sign players until January, so for the time being he is expected to play for the Juvenil - the under-18s.

Madrid also learned from the Martin Odegaard period that training with the first team while playing for the B side is a bad idea. So the plan is a spell in the B side, and when he is ready, Gabriel jumps straight into the first team.

Where Madrid are less happy is with how things have unfolded. Madrid wanted to set the timing themselves and be discreet, because they do not want problems with Manchester United and do not want to upset anyone. At Real Madrid, nobody is bigger than the club.

The idea was to keep everything quiet until January and announce it then. But with Gabriel already training in Madrid, the secret was never going to last.

"Players are moving to him because his reputation is that he'll get you a move to a bigger club," one Premier League club source told BBC Sport.

Dubai-based Barat does not just consider himself a super-agent, but a "boutique" super-agent.

Born in Iran and raised in London, Barat says he fell into football almost by accident after many years in international business.

After initially working as an intermediary at low-level clubs, he founded Epic Sports in January 2020.

His major football experience before that? The football game Championship Manager.

"I was always trading players," he told ESPN this year. "I was obsessed with every single player around the world."

This was not just about living out a fantasy in the real world. Barat was drawn into the profession because of the vast sums agents can earn in commission.

What makes his agency "boutique"? Unlike the top operations which have a huge number of players on their books, Epic Sports aims to have just 22 - two for each position.

This, Barat argues, ensures there is never any conflict of interest in how he represents his players.

Barat offers bespoke management of a player's career and came to prominence in the summer of 2025 when 15 of his players moved on.

This included Dean Huijsen joining Real Madrid, Nicolas Jackson moving to Bayern Munich and Xavi Simons signing for Tottenham Hotspur. Noni Madueke left Chelsea for Arsenal, and the Gunners signed Piero Hincapie.

This led to Barat being named Golden Boy Best Agent for the second time in three years.

Yet he is largely the figurehead, with agents working on his behalf around Europe. For instance, Epic has three other agents registered with the English Football Association (FA).

Barat, who also brokered Moises Caicedo's move to Chelsea, says he uses social media, and in particular influencer Fabrizio Romano, to amplify stories and agree transfers on his terms.

"Ali Barat redefines the game again," read an Epic Sports press release to announce Jackson's loan move to Bayern. No other agency seems to promote itself in this way.

The largely AI-generated video which announced Gabriel had joined Epic Sports was right on brand.

Gabriel's deal is part of a new venture: Epic Future - and this presents an ethical problem.

"It is about targeting the biggest young players, especially where they're not necessarily on the longest contracts," a Premier League source said. "And move them overseas for cheap fees.

"The original club will get a few 100,000 euros if that, and everyone else will hoover up millions and millions and millions - including his family."

Transferring a player to Europe also opens the door to future sell-on fees for an agent, which is against FA regulations.

It is this new focus on younger players which has started to cause friction at some top clubs.

No club wants to lose players they have spent years developing for nothing, only for an agent to reap the rewards.

Manchester United had to work hard 18 months ago to convince JJ Gabriel and his family that Old Trafford was the right place to further his football education.

The big question is, did they overpromise in doing so?

Sources close to the player eventually felt they were let down and United did not deliver on what was expected.

Certainly around Gabriel's pre-season minutes and presence in the squad for the Champions League opener against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK, which it was felt would be a perfect opportunity for the youngster to make his debut.

By the time the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton came round, there was no faith Gabriel would be brought on. Given United lost 3-2, there is merit in that stance.

The secondary elements are where will Gabriel develop the most?

United's academy is one of the best in England at producing young players, but given his size, will the forward benefit more from being in a less physical environment?

There has been a lot of sniping around his decision to leave United, but his stats are impressive and he is clearly a player of huge potential. United would certainly have wished the situation had not unfolded the way it has.

#731. Was The Rolling Stones’ 1973 Still Part of the Band’s Classic Period, Or the Beginning of the End? (Greatest Pop Stars Podcast)

This Vintage Pop Stardom episode of Greatest Pop Stars looks at a year where the World's Greatest Rock and Roll Band was at full power, but maybe moving into a different phase of its career.

In 1973, The Rolling Stones were coming off one of the greatest album runs in rock and roll history, a four-album stretch that cemented them as the World’s Greatest Rock and Roll Band, culminating in 1972’s Exile on Main Street and its legendarily hedonistic accompanying tour. Rather than take time off to victory lap following this iconic period, they headed to Jamaica to record their third album of the ’70s, released in 1973 as Goats Head Soup — which topped the Billboard 200 and spawned a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single with breakup ballad “Angie,” but drew middling lukewarm and is now viewed by many fans as the beginning of the end of the band’s glory days. Related 'What A Talent': Belinda Carlisle, UB40, Spandau Ballet & More Remember Andy Taylor U2 Wind Back the Years With Classics, Dolly Parton Tribute for Thanksgiving Eve NFL Halftime Show 'Hunger Games' Series Returns to No. 1 on Soundtracks Chart After More Than a Decade Explore The Rolling Stones See latest videos, charts and news

On this Vintage Pop Stardom episode of the Greatest Pop Stars podcast, host Andrew Unterberger is joined by Billboard executive digital director, east coast Joe Lynch — who wrote an excellent Stones cover story in July — to discuss a fascinating year in the Stones’ trajectory, where they were still one of the biggest bands in the world, but moving into their “holiday period” as rock standard-bearers.

Along the way, we answer all the most pressing questions about the 1973 Rolling Stones: Was Goats Head Soup really that much of a step down for the Stones, or is it a bit misunderstood historically? Is it surprising we didn’t get more of a reggae album out of it? What was the deal with that album title and album cover? Is “Angie” a little too MOR for our tastes? How much did the band go on to miss Mick Taylor (and/or Jimmy Miller) after their departures? Was Truman Capote really unable to find a story following the Stones on their single most storied tour? And perhaps most importantly: Why the hell are we doing the 1973 Rolling Stones for this podcast right now anyway?

#730. Aaron Rodgers Cut From Steelers After Slamming Coach Mike McCarthy

Aaron Rodgers criticized Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy after he was benched for the rest of the 2026 NFL season. The quarterback has since been cut from the team.

Aaron Rodgers' relationship with his coach entered the red zone.

The Pittsburgh Steelers player did not hold back about his opinion of coach Mike McCarthy after learning that he would be punting the title of starting quarterback. Rodgers lashed out at the NFL coach for surprisingly benching him for the NFL season—in favor of teammate Mason Rudolph—and has since been cut from the team.

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, that word never even came up," Rodgers revealed on Nov. 25 episode of The Pat McAfee Show, referring to "benching." He added that on a phone call with other team leadership he heard, "'I can't believe they're doing this,'" prompting him to ask, "'Doing what?' I didn't know."

And the former Green Bay Packer—who first worked with McCarthy for over a decade in Wisconsin—didn't toe the line when it came to detailing his issues with the 63-year-old, including a claim that McCarthy fell asleep during meetings.

"We were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers, 42, recounted. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers shared that his position stemmed from being "a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy," adding that McCarthy was "not coming to everything you should be coming to as a play caller."

That said, the Cal alum also stated McCarthy even missed meetings ahead of game day, such as before the Steelers' tough loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22.

And given Rodgers' concerns, he initiated a conversation about changes he believed were mandatory to move forward. In his words, he told McCarthy days before being deemed inactive, "'We got to make a change, like for the betterment of the team.’"

The Steelers later confirmed they cut Rodgers from the team, tweeting on Nov. 25, "We have released QB Aaron Rodgers.”

McCarthy declined to address the controversy with reporters on Nov. 25, but said he is the best person to lead the team.

"I know how to win, and that's the facts," he shared, per ESPN. "I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization, what we've got started and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today because of some of the things that frankly should have been talked about earlier. This is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of."

But it's not the first time Rodgers has tackled difficult subjects head-on. Read on for the NFL star's mindset about his complex relationship with his estranged family members, including his brother, Jordan Rodgers.

After growing up "in a really conservative, small-town environment" in Chico, Calif., Aaron Rodgers said in the Netflix docuseries Aaron Rodgers: Enigma, transferring from Butte College to University of California, Berkeley, was admittedly an eye-opening experience for him. "So that was fun, to have my ideologies tested."

But, as he recalled, he was already traveling a path that was taking him further and further away from how he was raised by dad Ed Rodgers and mom Darla Rodgers.

The "white, dogmatic church" he grew up in "didn’t really serve me," Aaron said. "It was very rigid in structure. I'm not a rigid person. Shame, guilt, judgment—it was like, 'We have the truth, our way or the highway, our way is heaven, your way is hell.' Even talking to my parents, it was very black and white. Somebody has to be wrong, somebody has to be right. I just slowly uncoupled from that in high school."

So being in a city like Berkeley "that challenged my beliefs" (and where he was sleeping in on Sunday after games instead of going to church), he continued, "definitely helped me to begin to question more things."

Desperately Seeking Spiritual Enlightenment

After capping off the Green Bay Packers' 2011-12 NFL season with a Super Bowl victory—which, until then, Aaron thought was the holy grail he was seeking—he started to wonder what else was out there.

"I really just desperately wanted to be more than  a football player," he said in the series, "and so I started my spiritual journey."

Aaron got into the teachings of progressive spiritual leader Rob Bell, author of What Is the Bible? (which the athlete is seen reading in the series), and started reading more philosophy and self-help books.

Appreciating what he found to be Rob's inclusive, nonjudgmental approach to faith, "He was a big help for me to totally unravel the religion of my youth," Aaron said in Enigma.

Through his readings, "I found a courage to speak my feelings better," he continued. "So I started to stand up to institutions of my youth, and that was everything from organized religion, my parents, dogma, ideology. That definitely changed the dynamics of my family, because I was just questioning all of it."

Winning a Super Bowl vaulted Aaron to another tier of fame, the athlete recalling how during the summer of 2011 he was "paparazzi'd" for the first time during a trip to Hawaii.

"I was like, 'F--k, life's different now," he said. And after he was on TV more, he added, "my whole ability to move around with relative anonymity changed."

He added, "I didn't do myself any favors with some of the girls I dated after that, that were in the public eye. I definitely hated it at first. Like really despised it. I enjoyed my private life. I enjoyed being able to go places. But from Super Bowl MVP, [league] MVP, State Farm commercials, that got a little more difficult."

While the doc flashed to pictures of him with three famous exes, that was the entirety of what Aaron said about his high-profile relationships with Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley (who, incidentally, he was engaged to and didn't just date).

Olivia, who dated Aaron from 2014 until 2017, denied rumors that she played a role in her ex's estrangement from his family, saying on Andy Cohen Live in 2018, "He hadn't spoken to the parents and one brother for, like, eight months before we started dating."

Aaron reiterated to biographer Ian O'Connor, author of 2024's Out of the Darkness: The Mystery of Aaron Rodgers, that his issues with his family were "deep rooted" and Olivia "has nothing to do with all the years" they haven't spoken.

"There was a lot of times, when I became real famous," Aaron said in Enigma, "where I heard from a lot of people, including family members, who where it was like, ‘Your life is too big, we need you to be smaller. Be smaller, don't talk about your life.'"

Feeling woefully misunderstood, he continued, "It always hurt me because I just feel like you don’t see me. This is not something I ever desired or wanted, other than playing on Sundays. It can definitely change the people around your circle, because it can be intoxicating, the fame and notoriety. So, definitely relationships changed after that. Friendships, family."

Aaron said that, pre-estrangement, he wasn't "super-duper close" with everybody in his family anyway.

"I was close with my little brother," he recalled, referring to younger sibling Jordan Rodgers. "But in actuality it goes back to stuff from high school that kind of made me feel distant. Stuff in college, stuff post-college. And I was quiet about it. 'Cause I thought the best way to do it was, just don’t talk about it publicly. And what do they do?"

In 2016, Jordan appeared on The Bachelorette—and, incidentally, he's been married to rose-bearer JoJo Fletcher since 2022.

When he brought JoJo home to meet his folks and eldest brother Luke Rodgers, there were two empty chairs at the dinner table—purportedly for Aaron and then-girlfriend Olivia—and all of a sudden millions of people found out the Packers QB was estranged from the rest of the family.

"We miss our brother," Luke said on The Bachelorette. "We just are trusting that God brings things full circle. And just wish that everything would just get back to us being a family."

"They go on a bulls--t show and leave two empty chairs," he said in Enigma. "They all agreed this was like a good thing to do, to leave two empty chairs at a stupid dating show that my brother just went on to get famous—his words, not mine—that he ended up winning."

Aaron reiterated in the series that he was never even invited to the dinner, which was held during the NFL season.

A dinner "I was never asked to go to," he said, "not that I would have gone."

E! News reached out to Jordan, Ed and Darla for comment on what Aaron had to say in Enigma but has not yet heard back.

Jordan told E! in 2016 after his hometown episode aired that he "made a commitment to go on there and be honest with JoJo and make sure that she knew everything" about where he was coming from.

Aaron has embraced taking ayahuasca—"It's the hardest medicine possible, that I've tried"—as an essential part of his journey, also touting its healing power for "mind, body, spirit."

"I was searching, for sure," he said in Enigma. "My life was through one lens, of organized religion. Where are people in life finding deep peace and centeredness and presence outside of what I knew?"

Speaking of the divide between him and his family, Aaron said he "found a lot of resistance" once he started researching other religions and plant medicine, "doing things that, compared to what I grew up in, would be considered an alternative lifestyle."

As for his family, he continued, "You know, they’re living as best they can. That is, still engulfed in organized religion, which works for them. That's great. So as much as they might not like what they see, love and respect and gratitude for how I was raised, because it wouldn’t have turned me into who I am today."

"People ask me, 'Is there hope for a reconciliation?'" Aaron said. "I say, 'Yeah, of course. Of course.'"

He added, "I don’t want them to fail, to struggle, to have any strife or issues. I don't wish any ill will on them at all. It's more like this: We're just different steps on the timeline of our own journeys."

#729. Inside the Madcap World of Chuyín: ‘Everyone Sings About the Neverending Party. I Sing About the Hangover’

Meet Billboard's Latin Up-and-Comer Artist of the Month for November.

At the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards last month, a mob of Chuyíns in white straitjackets turned the stage into a psychiatric ward during a performance of “Pues Ya Ni Pedo.” The show’s closing gag revealed members of Fuerza Regida beneath the oversized masks — a fitting glimpse into the wonderfully chaotic world of the música mexicana breakout star’s May debut album, Los Locos Nunca Mueren (Crazy People Never Die).

But to understand the mysterious masked performer, first enter the void.

“Before Chuyín, there was nothing, just black space,” the masked singer tells Billboard. According to his origin story, he came into existence on May 6, 2023, at a Fuerza Regida concert in Tepic, Nayarit, where frontman Jesús Ortiz Paz (JOP) “adopted” him. He’s been living with JOP ever since, he says, never once breaking character throughout the interview.

Chuyín is three years old — or 21, if you count in dog years, as he does — and already making his mark on música mexicana. His 16-track debut album, released May 7 via Street Mob Records, debuted at No. 9 on the Top Regional Mexican Albums chart and No. 17 on Top Latin Albums, both dated May 23. In September, “Pues Qué Le Hago?” gave him his first No. 1 on a Billboard chart, topping Regional Mexican Airplay.

On Los Locos Nunca Mueren, which features Fuerza Regida, Calle 24, Luis R Conriquez, Óscar Maydon and Jorsshh, Chuyín takes on the carnal pleasures and intoxicating excesses common to contemporary corridos — then gives them a comedic twist. His protagonist doesn’t escape the consequences.

On “Paniki,” a cheating Chuyín goes to ridiculous lengths to conceal his infidelity, only to get caught when he tries his luck again. On the album opener, “Rehabilitado,” he declares himself rehabilitated while remaining tempted by his vices.

“Everyone sings about the never-ending party. I sing about the hangover,” he says. “Everyone sings about partying, partying and partying. I sang about getting sent to rehab.”

Consequences are central to Chuyín’s character, but so is perseverance. “Chuyín is the guy everything happens to, and somehow he gets back up and keeps going,” he explains. “Everything that could go wrong happens to Chuyín, and he gets up with the same smile and says, ‘OK, let’s keep going.’”

Behind the irreverence is an emotionally invested songwriter. Chuyín says he wrote “Olvídate de Mí” entirely on his own while living through the failed relationship that inspired it. Rather than admit that he’s the problem, he tells his partner to forget him — and run if she knows what’s good for her.

The song reflects the openness he says defines the album. “If you listen to my music, you know me, and you don’t need to know anything else,” he says. “I give myself to the public completely, emotionally. And I think that’s what connected with people.”

For Chuyín, concealing his face affords him the freedom to bare his soul. “I feel like I’m mysterious, but I’m very vulnerable in my music,” he says. “It’s a beautiful thing that people can get to know you without you showing your face, because of what you sing about. I always sing about personal things I’ve experienced.”

With JOP as his mentor, Chuyín has honed his songwriting chops alongside Street Mob’s wider circle of creatives. “For me, writing music is like therapy,” he says. His songwriting extends beyond his own repertoire: He also helped pen Fuerza Regida’s “Tu Sancho.”

Onstage, Chuyín has experienced both the scale of a Fuerza stadium show and the intimacy of his own performance. Singing with the group at Mexico City’s Estadio GNP Seguros in front of an estimated 80,000 people was exhilarating, he says. But a solo Chuyín show in Chicago, where 800 people had come specifically to see him, felt even more personal.

“Both experiences were incredible, but they were very different,” he says. “Every one of those 800 people came just to see Chuyín.”

Name: Chuyín. Asked about the person behind the mask, he insists, “I’m Chuyín.”

Age: 3 — or 21 in Chuyín years. Each year counts as seven because Chuyín is “like a little dog,” he says.

Born and raised: Tepic, Nayarit, Mexico; Rancho Cucamonga, Calif.

Recommended song: “Olvídate de Mí,” a candid account of romantic self-sabotage that Chuyín says he penned entirely on his own.

Musical influences: His personal Mount Rushmore of música mexicana consists of Alfredo Olivas, Gerardo Ortiz, Natanael Cano and Junior H.

Major accomplishment: Scoring his first Billboard No. 1 with “Pues Qué Le Hago?,” which topped Regional Mexican Airplay in September. “I put all the love in the world into the music,” he says. “The fact that the public embraced it and that I made it onto the Billboard charts is crazy.”

What’s next: Chuyín is working on his sophomore album and exclusively reveals to Billboard that he will embark on his first headlining tour in 2027, with further details to be announced soon. The artist is preparing an immersive live show with one particularly mischievous tradition in mind: “At every show, I’m going to crown a Chuyín,” he says. “With every show, there will be one more Chuyín in this world.”

#728. Are Manchester United this season's Tottenham?

Manchester United are in the Premier League relegation zone 11 games into the season

Last season, Tottenham - a member of the so-called 'big six' - escaped relegation from the Premier League on the final day.

Now, with Manchester United making their worst start to a league season since 1972, it raises the question: are United this season's Spurs?

While Tottenham finished 17th with just 41 points last term, they actually started the season better than United have this season. After 11 games in 2025-26, Spurs were riding high in fifth with 18 points - 10 more than United have now.

But one of the biggest myths in football is 'the table never lies' and it was certainly lying about Tottenham at this stage last season.

While the table prompted talk of a possible Champions League place, expected goals (xG) had already recognised a relegation battle lay ahead for Tottenham, even predicting the position they'd finish in.

United's expected goal difference is almost identical to Tottenham's at this stage last season, but this time the table is more honest, even if United are perhaps not as bad as it makes out.

But there's no denying United's statistics are those of a team in a relegation battle, with many of them in the bottom six of Premier League teams this season.

While United have performed poorly defensively, their attack is actually not bad.

Remarkably, United have taken the most shots in the Premier League so far this season, and their expected goals scored figure is in the top five.

But what new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has to implement quickly is some quality control when it comes to shots at both ends of the pitch. United are converting just 7% of their chances and conceding 16% of their opponents' - a poor combination for any team.

And it is not simply down to finishing or shot-stopping, though they should have scored a few more. Based on xG per shot, United are currently taking the second-worst chances to score and giving up the easiest ones at the back.

As a result, Opta give United just over a one-in-four chance of being relegated at the end of the season (27.5%), making them the fifth-most likely side to go down after Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Ipswich and Coventry.

By analysing historical and team performances as well as the strength of opponents, Opta predict the percentage chance of each club finishing in each position.

While the above means it is more likely United will survive, it is worth noting the one position Opta predicts United are most likely to finish is 18th, with a 10.1% chance. That would mean the 13-time Premier League winners are relegated.

There is a 90% chance they finish anywhere else, but the next most likely are the three places just above the relegation zone, including a 9.9% chance of them finishing where Tottenham did last season.

History also suggests a relegation battle lies ahead for United given their poor start.

Of the 26 previous sides that had exactly eight points after 11 games, 13 survived and 13 were relegated. Among those that stayed up, only four finished more than six points above the danger zone.

A top-half finish looks unlikely. Since the competition became a 20-team league in 1995-96, no side has finished in the top half after taking eight points or fewer from their first 11 games.

Two teams did finish there more than 30 years ago but they had four more games to climb the table as teams played 42 games a season in those days.

Having said that, both were in the top half at the 38-game mark so United finishing there would not be entirely unprecedented.

It is a big ask, though, as the club have already taken 19 points fewer from the fixtures they have played than they did last season.

Even if they were to repeat the results that led to them finishing third from now on, they would still only reach 52 points, the number Chelsea narrowly finished 10th with last term.

Though United are without a win in nine Premier League matches, their remaining fixtures of 2026 do offer some hope.

While they have a tough home game against Brentford this weekend and a trip to champions Arsenal just before Christmas, their other five games are against teams currently in the bottom seven - sides we must, at this point, call relegation rivals.

So despite suffering the worst first game by a Manchester United manager for 100 years in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Pochettino will hope to quickly quash any concerns his new club will be embroiled in the same fight as his former one last season.

#721. Alan Bersten Speaks Out After Helping Ezra Frech When His Leg Fell Off

Dancing With the Stars pro Alan Bersten shared his reaction to Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach's win after he helped the duo when Frech's prosthetic leg flew off mid-dance.

Alan Bersten deserves the Mirrorball for best backup dancer.

The Dancing With the Stars pro proved he was Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach’s secret weapon during the Nov. 24 finale while performing during their freestyle routine to Linkin’ Park’s “Numb.” When the Paralympian’s prosthetic leg accidentally fell off mid-show, Bersten quickly grabbed the device and held it for safekeeping until Karagach could give it to Frech to reattach during the song. Plus, Bersten was locked into the choreography and didn’t even miss his cue to tear off Frech’s rip-away clothing.

Following Frech and Karagach’s win, Bersten shared how honored he was to have taken part in the dance alongside the duo.

“I just want to take a second and congratulate Ezra and Daniella,” he said in a Nov. 25 TikTok. “Ezra, your resilience and your composure and your courage is so inspiring.”

The 32-year-old—who was eliminated during week two alongside pro partner Giada De Laurentiis—added that the moment Frech reattached his leg mid-dance was one that “transcends Dancing with the Stars.”

“It's a moment that will live on forever,” he said. “And I hope you are so proud of yourself, Daniella. You've created something so magical. Congratulations, you guys.”

Karagach thanked her fellow pro for not only grabbing the prosthetic when it fell, but also for clearing away Frech’s tearaway suit from the stage so it wouldn’t get in their way.

“The way @alanbersten slid me that leg and made sure Ezra's rip away was cleared was true professionalism at its finest,” the 33-year-old posted to her Instagram Stories Nov. 24. “Grateful you had our backs. Can't thank you enough.”

The moment was also one that Frech himself would never forget as he recounted what was going through his mind the moment his prosthetic flew off.

“The leg just wasn't on correctly, and I felt it,” the 21-year-old told Variety following the episode. “Sometimes it'll readjust and I'll be okay. And so, as I was running up the steps, I'm like, ‘There's a 50 percent chance my leg will resuction and I'll be OK.’ And that wasn't the case.”

And while he was tempted to do the entire routine on one leg, he recalled hearing Karagach say, “‘Put your leg on,’ and I was like, ‘Yes, OK, yeah, good idea. I'll put it on right now.’”

Frech was able to reattach the limb before the duo gracefully jumped back into their routine, with Karagach explaining she quickly realized there was no other place in the dance that he could have taken a moment to reattach it.

“Nothing's better than him just clicking on his leg properly and continuing on with the dance,” she said. “I was like, ‘This is our only shot to do that.’”

Still, with all the adrenaline coursing through him, Frech actually had trouble remembering how exactly he got his prosthetic back.

“Did somebody give me the leg? Because I blacked out,” he asked aloud, to which Karagach confirmed she gave it to him. “You gave me the leg? Really?”

And as expected, the routine left its mark on the series, with judge Derek Hough telling the dancing duo, “This performance will have a ripple effect far beyond this show. What you did tonight was forever. Kids will look up to you and see what's possible."

The NFL Thanksgiving Day Game happens on Thursday (Nov. 26) with a matchup featuring the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) taking on the Dallas Cowboys (4-6) at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, with a start time of 4:30 p.m. ET/1:30 p.m. PT.

The Eagles-Cowboys game broadcasts on FOX, while the NFL game is available to livestream on FOX One.

NFL games are known for celebrity sightings, so it’s likely there may be a number of famous actors, actresses and recording artists in attendance. Artists have been known to appear at games in the past, include Cowboys fans Post Malone, Selena Gomez, Eva Longoria and others.

Additionally, Miranda Lambert performs at halftime, which starts around 6 p.m. ET/3 p.m. PT.

Plus, contemporary Christian music singer-songwriter Lauren Daigle is set to perform the National Anthem, “The Star-Spangled Banner.”

For cord-cutters, there are a few ways to watch the NFL Thanksgiving Day Game if you don’t have cable, especially if you want to watch for free. DirecTV has a five-day free trial, while other streaming services offer free trials, so you can watch the Eagles vs. Cowboys for free.

A subscription to DirecTV gets you access to live TV, local and cable channels, including FOX, at $49.99 per month for the two first months of service ($94.99 per month afterward). The service even offers a five-day trial to watch for free, if you sign up now. It comes with access to ESPN Unlimited too for even more ESPN networks.

Sling Blue comes with 40+ broadcast and cable channels.

Sling TV offers the Blue plan, which comes with FOX. With more than 40 channels, the streaming plan goes for $54.99 per month. All plans come with a free cloud DVR and an extra 600 or so free channels too. Please note: Pricing and channel availability vary from market-to-market.

Fubo is an affordable option offering a five-day free trial for new users who sign up.

Fubo starts at $63.99 for the first month ($88.99 per month afterward) with more than 230 channels, including local and cable networks, like FOX, that are streamable on smart TVs, smartphones, tablets and on web browsers. And with a five-day free trial, you can watch for free if you act fast and sign up now.

Comes with Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select.

For the NFL Thanksgiving Day Game: Eagles vs. Cowboys, the broadcast network FOX is available to watch with Hulu + Live TV. Pricing for the cable alternative starts at $99.99 per month for more than 100 live channels, while each plan comes with Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select at no additional cost. Hulu + Live TV might be best for those who want all of these streaming services together in one package.

With prices starting at $19.99 per month, FOX One is your one-stop app for everything FOX has to offer, including streaming access to FOX. It also includes FS1, FS2, Big Ten Network, FOX News, FOX Business, FOX Nation, FOX Weather, FOX Deportes and your local FOX broadcasting affiliate.

Prime Video has a three-day free trial available for Amazon Prime members, so you watch FOX One as an add-on to Amazon’s streaming service.

Not a member?
